_meta.indication: Adjunctive treatment of adult patients with severe active ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA and MPA) in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids; TAVNEOS does not eliminate glucocorticoid use.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial comparing avacopan 30 mg twice daily to a prednisone taper (60 mg/day to 0 over 20 weeks), all on background standard immunosuppression (rituximab or cyclophosphamide/azathioprine).
pivotal_trials.population: 330 adults with newly diagnosed or relapsed ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA and MPA), randomized 1:1.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: disease remission at Week 26 and sustained disease remission at Week 52 (BVAS of 0 with no glucocorticoid use).
pivotal_trials.result: Remission at Week 26: 72.3% avacopan vs 70.1% prednisone (treatment difference 3.4%, 95% CI [-6.0%, 12.8%]) — non-inferior. Sustained remission at Week 52: 65.7% vs 54.9% (treatment difference 12.5%, 95% CI [2.6, 22.3]; p=0.013) — superior.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): nausea (23.5% vs 20.7%), headache (20.5% vs 14.0%), hypertension (18.1% vs 17.7%), diarrhea, vomiting, rash. Serious hepatic injury and elevated liver function tests occurred more frequently with TAVNEOS; hepatic-related AEs occurred in 13.3% of TAVNEOS patients vs 11.6% of prednisone patients.
target_moa: Avacopan is a small molecule antagonist of the complement 5a receptor (C5aR), blocking C5a-mediated neutrophil chemoattraction and activation implicated in ANCA-associated vasculitis.

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee met May 6, 2021. On whether efficacy data support approval, the committee split 9 Yes / 9 No; on whether the safety profile is adequate to support approval, 10 Yes / 8 No; on whether the benefit-risk profile is adequate to support approval at the proposed dose of 30 mg twice daily, 10 Yes / 8 No.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation granted by FDA on June 2, 2014 for the treatment of ANCA-associated vasculitides (GPA/Wegener's granulomatosis, microscopic polyangiitis, and Churg-Strauss syndrome/EGPA).

avacopan was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies associated vasculitides (granulomatosis with polyangiitis or Wegener's granulomatosis), microscopic polyangiitis, and Churg-Strauss syndrome (EGPA)

summary.text: TAVNEOS (avacopan) was reviewed under a Standard (non-priority) review of NDA 214487, and was granted Orphan Drug designation for ANCA-associated vasculitis. It was not an accelerated approval. An Arthritis Advisory Committee was convened on May 6, 2021, at which the committee was split, and the drug was approved with postmarketing requirements/commitments for long-term safety, efficacy, and drug-interaction studies.

requirement.text: 4155-1: Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in ANCA-associated vasculitis patients to evaluate safety outcomes, including hepatotoxicity/drug-induced liver injury and serious hypersensitivity reactions (angioedema and anaphylaxis).

citations.quote: 4155-1 Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in patients with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis to evaluate safety outcomes, including hepatotoxicity and drug-induced liver injury, and serious hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema and anaphylaxis.

requirement.text: 4155-2: Conduct a clinical drug interaction trial evaluating the effect of repeated doses of avacopan 30 mg twice daily with food at steady state on the PK of a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate (e.g., simvastatin).

citations.quote: 4155-2 Conduct a clinical drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of repeated doses of avacopan 30 mg twice daily with food at steady state on the pharmacokinetics of a sensitive substrate of CYP3A4 (e.g., simvastatin) to inform appropriate dosing strategies for coadministration of avacopan with CYP3A4 substrates.

requirement.text: 4155-3: Conduct a randomized controlled clinical trial of at least five years duration in ANCA-associated vasculitis patients to evaluate efficacy outcomes with long-term avacopan treatment.
